en.headline: Jason Poon and wife granted bail over alleged HK$6m loan fraud
en.dek: The construction businessman and his wife face fraud and money-laundering charges linked to a Covid-era SME financing scheme; the case will move to the District Court.
body: Businessman Jason Poon Chuk-hung and his wife Carrie Chu Shu-fong were granted bail at Kowloon City Court on Monday after being charged over an alleged HK$6 million fraud involving a government SME financing scheme during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Magistrate Arthur Lam Hei-wei set cash bail of HK$100,000 each and ordered the pair to remain in Hong Kong and report weekly to police. The fraud and money-laundering proceedings will be transferred to the District Court, where the maximum total sentence for the charges is seven years.

Poon, 56, a construction businessman, and Chu, 54, are due to return to Kowloon City Court on 2 November for documentation related to the transfer. They are expected to enter pleas at the District Court at a later date.

zh.headline: 潘焯鴻夫婦涉600萬元貸款詐騙獲保釋
zh.dek: 建築商人潘焯鴻及妻子被控涉及疫情期間中小企融資擔保計劃詐騙及洗黑錢，案件將轉介區域法院審理。
body: 建築商人潘焯鴻及其妻子朱瑞芳周一在九龍城裁判法院提堂，被控涉及疫情期間一項中小企融資擔保計劃約600萬元詐騙及洗黑錢，裁判官林熙維批准各以10萬元現金保釋。
兩人須留在香港，並每周向警方報到。案件將轉介區域法院，該院對有關控罪的最高總刑期為七年。
56歲的潘焯鴻及54歲的朱瑞芳須於11月2日再返九龍城裁判法院處理轉介文件，其後預期在區域法院答辯。
